This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **5** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/ui.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/ui.json`, `packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/ui.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/ui.json`, `packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **142** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a7a135dc267f0d154aca453f098c49ce8aac550c` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `543d9f315c7e97cc8526f20a83f5ef662c7d126a` — the merge of head `dce5433072dcd82b591b3fc3831927cf1cbc0007` into base `a7a135dc267f0d154aca453f098c49ce8aac550c`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 543d9f315c7e97cc8526f20a83f5ef662c7d126a && git checkout 543d9f315c7e97cc8526f20a83f5ef662c7d126a
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin a7a135dc267f0d154aca453f098c49ce8aac550c dce5433072dcd82b591b3fc3831927cf1cbc0007 && git checkout -B drift-repro a7a135dc267f0d154aca453f098c49ce8aac550c && git merge --no-ff dce5433072dcd82b591b3fc3831927cf1cbc0007

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a7a135dc267f0d154aca453f098c49ce8aac550c
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs a7a135dc267f0d154aca453f098c49ce8aac550c` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `dce5433072dcd82b591b3fc3831927cf1cbc0007`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #23357 (body; comments `6159116611` triage, `6160762995` claim amended in place, `6163363165` seat-3 pointer, `6164084655` regrade, `6164488810` os-dev-report, `6164621776` ACCEPT); PR #23419 body, its 11-file list and the net diff against the merge-base `c857a93ee` (+493/-17); the check-runs on `dce543307` and on the prior head `63e1e4800` (differs by one changeset line, the `Clause-②` arm); the committed source on `origin/claude/issue-23357-page-component-api-data` and `origin/main`. Nothing was built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

**(a) The narrowing — right.** `checkPageComponentViewData` (page.zod.ts, the fifth `PageSchema` object-level check) fires only when a node's `type` is one of `object-grid` / `object-map` / `object-gantt` / `object-tree`, its `properties` is a non-array object, and `properties.data` is an object whose `provider` is strictly `'api'`. It then runs `ViewDataSchema.safeParse(data)` and raises the issue found at path `provider`. Three things judged:
- *Exactly the retired spelling, nothing else in the bag.* The `=== 'api'` gate means another provider (`object`, `value`, `schema`, an unknown `rest`), a missing `data`, a bare-array `data`, a row-array type carrying the binding (`object-kanban`), a type with no props row (`custom:partner-widget`) and the component's own governed `dataSource: { provider: 'api', read: { url } }` (`ElementApiDataSourceSchema`, outside `properties`) are all untouched; each is a pinned control in `page-component-view-data.test.ts` and the parity fixtures. The view's union `error` map (view.zod.ts:277-285) returns the prescription only when `input.provider === 'api'`, so an uppercase or other misspelling meets zod's default report in both places, consistently.
- *Read, not copied.* `VIEW_DATA_API_PROVIDER_RETIRED` is a module-private `const` in view.zod.ts, so page.zod.ts cannot import it; the check raises `retirement.message` off the view's own issue, and if the view ever re-admits the arm (`verdict.success`) the page check falls silent with it. The `PRESCRIPTION` in the pins is likewise read off `ViewDataSchema` with an anti-vacuity assertion.
- *Path.* `[...path, 'properties', 'data', 'provider']`, pinned at a region component, a `page:tabs` item child, a container grandchild, `slots.header.0` and `slots.details`; the save door reports the same string path (`regions.0.components.0.properties.data.provider`).
- *Issue code.* `custom`, not the view's `invalid_union`: the parity harness (`runParse`) treats any non-`custom` issue as "fixture not shape-valid" and throws, so `custom` is the only code an object-level check on `PageSchema` may raise. Message byte-identical. Right.

**(b) The reach — right.** `definePage` is `PageSchema.parse` (page.zod.ts:1855) and is pinned to throw. `defineStack` parses through `ObjectStackDefinitionSchema.safeParse` (stack.zod.ts), whose `pages` is `z.array(PageSchema)` (:496) and which `ObjectStackSchema` aliases by identity (:1888); the pin is on `ObjectStackSchema.safeParse({ pages })`, which is the same schema object, so `defineStack` is covered transitively though not called by name in a pin. The `page` metadata type's schema is `PageSchema` by identity (metadata-type-schemas.ts:113), which `resolveOverlaySchema` resolves for the save door (protocol.ts:813-815); `protocol.save-union-issues.test.ts` pins `422 INVALID_METADATA`, nothing persisted, the located `custom` issue, top-level and `page:tabs`-nested, with `object` and `value` controls that persist one row. The stored-page consequence: `loadMetaFromDb` is "Diagnose, never drop … STILL registered" with the `[metadata_spec_invalid]` warning (protocol.ts:28973-28984, :29104); the read path is pinned for a page (`_diagnostics.valid` false, prescription at the path). The register-anyway rule is pinned on an `object` row (`protocol.stored-conversions.test.ts:286-293`, `loaded 1 / invalid 1 / registered`); the page-specific boot count `loaded 2 / invalid 1` was measured with a deleted probe only. The fate text is right on the protocol's one type-agnostic rule; a page row in that boot pin would close the last gap (follow-up, not a blocker).

**(c) The hand-declared set — holds over the map's domain; one direction has a blind spot.** `VIEW_DATA_SOURCE_COMPONENT_TYPES` is a module-private set of the four; the import-cycle reason is measured (component.zod.ts:89 imports `ElementDataSourceSchema` and `RETIRED_PAGE_COMPONENT_TYPES` from page.zod.ts). The derivation pin compares `_zod.def` identity of each row's unwrapped `data` member to `ViewDataSchema`'s (the `lazySchema` proxy inherits the real def, so identity is sound) and asserts exactly the four with an anti-vacuity floor of 40 rows; the behavioural pin asserts, for every `ComponentPropsMap` key, refused-at-position if and only if the row takes `ViewDataSchema`. So set ∩ map-keys equals the derivation in both directions. What neither pin can see: a name added to the hand set that is not a `ComponentPropsMap` key at all (a custom or registered block). The set is private, so no pin enumerates it; the guard is review of page.zod.ts. At this head the set is the four, so the contract is right. Precision note on the "both directions" claim, not a defect.

**(d) The generic walk — it can refuse one contrived non-component shape.** The walk descends every object and array under `regions` and `slots`, including the whole of a component's open `properties`: `data.items` (the `value` arm's `z.array(z.unknown())`), `staticData`, `read.headers`. A static row or any open-record value that itself spells `type` in the four and `properties.data.provider: 'api'` is refused at its own path, though it is data, not a component. The listing (`mapPageComponents`, walk.ts:304-330) descends only `pageComponentSlotPositions()` keys, and the props row's `items` is `z.unknown()`, so neither would refuse that site: in that corner the page parse is strictly narrower than both. Reachable only by authoring a row that is itself a retired component spelling; the refusal when it fires is the correct prescription at a located path, never a silent change; and the `refused-shapes.test.ts` "exactly the listed positions" pin bounds the walk only for its fixture. Superset claim confirmed: every slot position (`children`, `items[].children`, the retired container spellings) is a plain descent, so nothing the listing lists is missed. The `seen` identity set ends a self-referencing hand-built stack (pinned). No `PageComponentSchema` alias exists for `properties`, so an unparsed nested child cannot hide behind one. Residual recorded; not a FAIL.

**(e) The new published export — right.** `export function checkPageComponentViewData` in page.zod.ts, attached once by identifier after `checkPageSlotPair`; the `ui` barrel re-exports page.zod (index.ts:53); `api-surface/ui.json` and `export-origins/ui.json` each gain exactly the one alphabetically placed line; `object-refinement-check-exports.test.ts` pins declaration count 1, attachment count 1, the barrel's reference identity, and the `(value, ctx)` arity. `check:api-surface`, `check:export-origins`, `check:generated` (14 artifacts) exit 0 in the report; the Lint jobs that host them are green on both heads.

The scope was registered at #23082; this diff moves enforcement onto the page parse and updates `acceptanceCriteria` to name every door that parses a page, the save door's 422 included. No new entry owed. The gate runs in `Check Changeset` ("Require an ADR-0087 disposition on a declared-breaking changeset", pr-automation.yml), success twice on `dce543307`; exit 0 locally per the report. Right.
- **`Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`** reads identically in the claim (`6160762995`, amended in place 08:48Z), the PR body's line 3, and the changeset at `dce543307` (the one-line delta from `63e1e4800`). One arm, as the rule requires: `yes` for the export, `(narrowing)` for the accept set. Right.
